title: Steward Countdown Cookbook — Microcohort Ops Scratchpad
content:
Purpose: capture a compact, operational-ready ritual for running microcohort canaries and A/B slices that leans into human steward rhythms (countdown, handoffs, escalation) rather than heavyweight runbooks. Intent is to be short, actionable, and easy-to-follow during an activation window.

Context + motivation:
- We frequently run small-slice LLM feature launches where behavioral drift shows up in subtle ways (tone, hallucination rate, rerank flips). Ops time is limited; we need a ritual that is fast to perform and yields signal quickly.
- This doc focuses on microcohort steward choreography (who does what and when), a compact telemetry checklist, and a short set of recovery actions.

Core idea: Steward Countdown (T-24h -> activation -> T+48h)
- T-24h: Bake hypothesis + safety slices. One steward (primary) prepares: 3 key metrics, two sentinel user journeys, error budget threshold. Share Slack thread with pin.
- T-2h: Dry run synthetic traffic (5k synthetic calls) with golden prompts, verify latency & token-cost baseline. Primary posts quick pass/fail.
- T-0: Activation window start. Primary moves traffic to slice (targeted cohort). Secondary monitors telemetry dashboards. Triage channel opened (#rollout-steward).
- T+2h: Early heuristic pass. If any sentinel metric exceeds threshold, immediate mitigation options executed (see Mitigation list).
- T+12h: Manual quality sweep with sample of 200 real responses; steward tags 10% for deeper review.
- T+48h: Decision checkpoint. Either continue ramp, pause and rollback, or escalate to emergency oncall.

Suggested metrics (pick top 3):
- Safety delta: percent change in hallucination rate (labeling heuristics) vs baseline.
- Acceptance funnel: percent drop in user continuation / conversion within same session after changed behavior.
- Prompt-to-first-token latency P95 and cost-per-1k tokens delta.
- Functional regressions: rerank consistency rate (top-1 flips) for sample queries.

Telemetry quick queries (examples, adapt to our internal schema):
- hallucination_rate = SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE flagged_hallucination) / count(*) FROM responses WHERE cohort = 'micro' AND ts >= now() - interval '6 hours';
- top1_flip_rate = SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE top1_new != top1_base) / count(*) FROM rerank_checks WHERE ts >= now() - interval '12 hours';
- latency_p95 = percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) FROM requests WHERE route = 'chat' AND cohort = 'micro';
(These are illustrative; implementers: map fields to our telemetry names.)

Slice definitions (practical examples):
- microcohort-A: 1% of signed-in users from NA desktop with locale=en-US, low-frequency heavy-prompting (>2k tokens/session).
- microcohort-B: 0.5% of mobile users in EU beta group (privacy opt-in).

Steward roles & cadence (short):
- Primary steward: prepares artifacts, triggers activation, runs T+2h/12h checks, decides on pause.
- Secondary steward: acts as verifier, runs manual quality sweep, coordinate rollback if asked.
- Escalation steward (oncall): takes final action if automatic mitigations fail or metrics breach emergency thresholds.
- Communication steward: writes the short public note for impacted teams and CS.

Mitigation playbook (fast actions):
1) Soft-fallback: switch cohort to more conservative model variant (same model family, smaller temperature).
2) Token-shedding: cap max tokens for that cohort for next 1h.
3) Throttle: reduce traffic share by 90% immediately, continue sampling 1:100 for signal.
4) Rollback: route cohort to pre-activation config and mark rollout as paused.
5) Hotfix: apply prompt patch or guardrail transform (if trivial).

Decision rubric (T+48h):
- Continue ramp if all top-3 metrics are within +/- 5% of baseline and no safety flags.
- Pause & mitigate if any safety metric > 10% delta or user-funnel drop > 7%.
- Escalate if hallucination rate > 20% higher than baseline or any outright P0 safety incident.

Quick checklist for activation thread:
- Hypothesis one-liner + success metric
- Link to telemetry dashboards + query snippets
- Primary/secondary/escalation names and contact links
- Synthetic dry-run pass (Y/N)
- Intended ramp plan (1% -> 5% -> 20% with durations)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Authorize a single canonical metric for hallucination detection (labeler vs heuristic).
- Add a tiny UI affordance in Console to enable "steward countdown mode" that automatically posts the T- timers and reminders.
- Define how cost caps interact with rollout (automated throttles vs alert-only).

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Next: prototype a Slack ritual bot that posts T-24/T-2/T+2/T+12 reminders and provides one-click mitigation toggles to the steward.
- Parking lot: create a short training deck (10 slides) for new stewards.

——
This document is intentionally terse. Use it as a quick operational checklist rather than the canonical encyclopedic playbook. Update with implementation names/IDs before running any activation.
